body:
# Independent audit of the square-root-tail and packing argument

The following scalar conclusion is proved by the argument audited here:
for every finite positive concave sequence at consecutive integer indices,
with integer weighted mean translated to zero, and for every integer `h>=0`,

    sum_(i>h) w_i >= [M-(2h+1)m]/3,
    sum_(i<-h) w_i >= [M-(2h+1)m]/3,              (1)

where `M=sum w_i` and `m=max w_i`. A negative right-hand side is
automatically harmless. The only nontrivial imported scalar fact is the
proved square-root concavity of the tail sums of a positive concave
sequence, on its actual positive indices. No artificial zero endpoint
is used below.

## 1. The maximum-atom bound and small supports

For `N>=5` terms and an interior maximum at index `j`, the two chords
from the peak to zero at the original endpoint indices lie below the
positive sequence. Summing them and subtracting the peak counted twice
gives `M>=(N-1)m/2>=2m`. If the peak is an endpoint, its chord to zero
at the other endpoint gives `M>=Nm/2`.

For `N=4`, reflection and integer translation put the indices at
`-1,0,1,2`. Write the widths `(a,b,c,e)`. Mean zero and concavity give

    a=c+2e,   c+e<=b<=2c-e,   M=b+2c+3e.

Then

    M-2a=b-e>=c>0,
    M-2b>=4e>0,
    M-2c=b+3e>0,
    M-2e=b+2c+e>0.

Thus for every `N>=4`, `mu:=m/M<=1/2`.

A one-term sequence has only index zero and (1) is immediate. Two
positive consecutive terms cannot have an integer mean. Three positive
terms must have middle index zero and widths `(a,b,a)`, with `b>=a`.
For `h=0`, the tail is `a>=(M-m)/3=2a/3`; for `h>=1`, the right-hand
side of (1) is nonpositive. These observations settle all small supports.

## 2. A uniform bound on the right tail's first moment

Assume `N>=4`, fix `h>=0`, and suppose toward a contradiction that

    T:=sum_(i>h) w_i < [M-(2h+1)m]/3.

In particular `T<M/3`. When `T>0`, let `F_j=sum_(i>=j) w_i` and set
`c=m/(2 sqrt(M))`. Except for a one-term tail, we claim

    F_(h+k) <= (sqrt(T)-(k-1)c)_+^2,   k>=1.       (2)

Let `p` be an index where `w_p=m`, and let `R` be the final positive
index. If `p<=h+1` and `p<R`, square-root-tail concavity makes the
decrements `delta_j=sqrt(F_j)-sqrt(F_(j+1))` nondecreasing for
`p<=j<R`. Moreover

    delta_p=m/(sqrt(F_p)+sqrt(F_(p+1)))>=c.

This gives (2) on every subsequent positive tail index.

If `p>h+1`, concavity of the widths gives `w_(h+1)>=w_0`. Jensen
with the centered weights `w_i/M`, together with the previously proved
strict quadratic inequality, gives `w_0>=Q/M>2m/3`. Therefore

    delta_(h+1)>=w_(h+1)/(2 sqrt(T))
                  >m/(3 sqrt(T))>m/(2 sqrt(M))=c,

where the last inequality uses `T<M/3<4M/9`. Tail concavity again
propagates this decrement bound to the right.

The only remaining peak case is `p=R=h+1`, when the tail has one term.
Its first excess moment is simply `T`, and the bound needed below is
automatic. Thus no undefined decrement at the last positive index is
taken. In the other cases, after the last positive index set `F_j=0`;
inequality (2) is then automatic and does not invoke concavity at an
appended zero. On each positive index the right side before squaring
must be positive, since it bounds the positive square root from above.

Summing (2), or using the one-term observation, bounds the right first
excess moment by

    E:=sum_(i>h)(i-h)w_i
       =sum_(k>=1) F_(h+k)
       <=T+integral_0^infinity (sqrt(T)-c x)_+^2 dx
        =T+2 sqrt(M) T^(3/2)/(3m).                   (3)

The sum-to-integral direction is correct because the integrand is
nonnegative and decreasing. For `T=0`, (3) is immediate as well.

## 3. The exact discrete packing bound on the other side

Put `L=M-T`. Among masses of size at most `m` at indices at most `h`,
the maximal first moment is obtained by filling `h,h-1,...` in order.
Writing `L=q m+r` with integer `q>=0` and `0<=r<m`, this gives

    sum_(i<=h) i w_i
       <=hL-m q(q-1)/2-q r
       <=hL-L^2/(2m)+L/2.                           (4)

The second upper bound exceeds the exact first bound by
`r(m-r)/(2m)>=0`. Enlarging the available index set to all integers
at most `h` only enlarges the maximum, so finite support causes no issue.

Combining the true zero moment with (3) and (4) yields

    0<=hM-(M-T)^2/(2m)+(M-T)/2
                           +T+2 sqrt(M)T^(3/2)/(3m).

Set `t=T/M`, `mu=m/M`, and `s=(h+1/2)mu`. Rearrangement is exactly

    s >= (1-t)^2/2-(2/3)t^(3/2)-mu t/2.             (5)

The alleged counterexample requires `s<(1-3t)/2`. For `t>0`, the
right side of (5) minus `(1-3t)/2` is

    t[1/2+t/2-(2/3)sqrt(t)-mu/2].

The quadratic `1/2+x^2/2-2x/3` has global minimum `5/18`, and
`mu<=1/2`. Hence the bracket is at least `1/36>0`, contradicting
the counterexample condition. If `t=0`, (5) says `s>=1/2`, again
contradicting `s<1/2`. This proves the right inequality in (1), and
reflection proves the left one.

All signs, normalizations, final-index cases, and the exact discrete
packing correction pass independent audit. This argument removes the
need to import the separate sharp open-tail `3/7` certificate. Combined
with the independently audited symmetric-proper-block reduction and
the two chord arguments, it supplies their previously missing captured
tail estimate; it makes no assertion in higher continuous dimension.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
